title: Inquest to begin next month in death of 26-year-old Cambridge man
article: An inquest into the death of Cambridge's Kieran Kay will begin on March 9.

The 26-year-old died in hospital on May 22, 2017, while in the custody of the Waterloo Regional Police Service. An inquest is mandatory under the Coroners Act. The inquest will examine the circumstances surrounding Kay's death and the jury may make recommendations aimed at preventing further deaths.

In an Special Investigations Unit news release after Kay's death, it was reported paramedics arrived first at a house on Day Street, in the area of Cedar Street and Southgate Road. Kay's stepfather said, as per the SIU investigation, he called 911 and Kay appeared to be high on drugs. He then tried to contain his stepson and hold him against the couch until police arrived.

Paramedics waited in the kitchen until police arrived moments later, the stepfather said, and then handcuffs were placed on Kay before paramedics checked his condition and soon realized his vital signs were absent.
After medical treatment, he was taken to hospital where he was pronounced dead, SIU stated in their release.
The inquest is expected to last five days and hear from 10 witnesses.
The inquest will start at 9:30 a.m. at the Ontario Court of Justice, 85 Frederick St.
